title: LineHound Hounds: the AI hounds
disclaimer: Paper-only. A language model reads the board an hour before each game and bets or passes (the Gematria Hound asks no model: it counts numerological coincidences by a fixed rule). No edge or profit is claimed.

council.note: Parked until a second model is enabled in config/ai_providers.json. Set the Council Hound's enabled flag below to true to run it; it needs at least min_members members that returned a valid answer for a game.

hounds.name: Claude Hound
hounds.tagline: A language model reads the board an hour before the game.
hounds.style: language model reads the board at lock
hounds.rule_text: Every sport we capture (the whole dog menu: baseball, football, basketball, hockey, soccer, tennis, MMA, cricket, rugby and the rest), moneyline everywhere and spread or total only where we capture them (tennis and MMA are moneyline only; soccer is moneyline and total, three-way, and a draw loses a team moneyline). An hour before the game, Claude Haiku 5.5 is shown only the board as it stood then (teams, each book's prices, the average and best price, the books' de-vigged number, how the moneyline moved since it opened) and, for MLB and NFL, the clubs' recent results from our stores (other sports get prices and movement only, and the packet says so), and answers bet or pass with a side, a confidence from 1 to 5 and a reason of 25 words or fewer. Code bets one unit on its answer only if the market is on the board and the average price is better than -200 (never -200 or worse), at most 3 bets a day. If the model is down, over its monthly cap or gives an answer that is not valid, the hound passes. Forward only: it is never replayed over old games. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

persona.bio: A very well-read hound who has never once been right about a game he was not shown. Gets the board an hour out, a 25-word allowance, and no memory of how any of it ends.
persona.catchphrase: The board says what it says.
roasts: Twenty-five words of reasoning and the game used none of them.
Read the whole board, confident at four out of five, wrong at five out of five.
A hound that has read everything and still cannot beat the closing line. Interesting.
The model was sure. The scoreboard was not consulted.
Passing was an option. It is always an option.
brags: The board was clear for once. Do not frame this.
Read it, said it, cashed it. Do not ask it to do that twice.
A confident four, and the game agreed. It will not last.
Twenty-five words well spent. One night's worth.
Fine. The reading hound read it right.
persona.epitaph: Read every board and never saw a result coming.

hounds.name: Council Hound
hounds.tagline: Only bets when most of the models agree.
hounds.rule_text: Every sport the model hounds cover. Asks no model itself. For each game it reads the answers the model hounds gave at the lock and bets only when at least 3 of them returned a valid answer and a strict majority of those backed the same side (home or away, over or under), in the market most of them chose. Same price rules as the model hounds: never -200 or worse, at most 3 bets a day. Forward only. Paper only.

persona.bio: Chairs a committee of language models and only acts when the room agrees. Has never been alone in a decision and has never claimed to be right.
roasts: A majority of models agreed and the game did not attend the meeting.
Three models, one opinion, zero units.
The committee voted. The scoreboard overruled.
brags: The room agreed and the game agreed with the room. Adjourned.
Motion carried and it cashed. Record that.
Consensus paid tonight. Do not make it a policy.
The committee got one right. Note the date.
persona.epitaph: Adjourned for lack of a majority.
persona.verb: put it to a vote and took

hounds.name: Gematria Hound
hounds.tagline: Experimental numerology hound. Paper picks, graded in public like every hound.
hounds.style: counts numerical coincidences for each side
hounds.rule_text: Every sport we capture, moneyline only. An hour before the game it works out, for each team, what the numbers would say if that team won: the cipher values of the team's name, city, mascot, state, university and head coach (English Ordinal, Full Reduction and their reverses), the number of the day and date, how far the game is from a founding or statehood date, and the counts a win would produce from our stored results (win and loss totals, streaks, days since the last win or loss, head-to-head, an NFL coach's record with the club). Every time one of those numbers equals another, or is the Nth prime or triangular number of another, or is 33 or 47, that is one piece of evidence, weighted by a fixed table (config/gematria/rules_v1.json). It bets the side with the larger total only if it leads by at least 3.0, both sides had enough stored results to count, and the side's average price is better than -200 (the band is -199 to +400); otherwise it passes and logs why. At most 3 bets a day, one unit, lock-time board and stored results only. The rules are versioned and never edited after a pick is made. Experimental and unproven: nothing here claims that numerology predicts games; the record is the only evidence.

persona.bio: Counts. Everything. The date, the founding year, the third letter of the coach, the number of the state. Has never been asked how many of the numbers it counted were going to match anyway.
persona.catchphrase: The numbers line up. Whether that means anything is the whole experiment.
roasts: Found eleven matches. Searched four hundred places.
Every number lined up. The game used different ones.
It counted the founding date down to the day and the day did not care.
Nine coincidences for one side, eight for the other, zero for the scoreboard.
The prime was prime. The pick was not.
brags: The numbers lined up and so did the score. Do not read anything into it.
A margin of four and a win. The sample is still one.
It counted, it picked, it cashed. Ask again in a hundred games.
That one lined up. The search was big enough that some will.
Right this time, and the record will say how often.
persona.epitaph: Found a pattern in everything and in nothing.
